---
title: "Wellness"
description: "Support the physical and environmental basics that make other skills easier to use."
---

::: {.tsk-page-lede}
Wellness skills are not a cure-all. They are capacity supports. When sleep, food, movement, medication routines, or the environment are seriously disrupted, every other coping skill can become harder to access.
:::

## Basic-needs check {#basic-needs-check}

Before interpreting a difficult moment only as a psychological problem, check the basics:

- Have I eaten enough for the part of the day I am in?
- Have I had water?
- Am I exhausted or significantly sleep deprived?
- Am I physically ill, in pain, overheated, or very cold?
- Have I taken prescribed medication as directed, if applicable?
- Have I been isolated or overstimulated for a long time?

Choose one correctable item rather than trying to optimize everything at once.

## Sleep routine {#sleep-routine}

A useful sleep routine focuses on repeatable cues rather than forcing sleep.

Try keeping the wake time reasonably consistent, reducing stimulating tasks close to bedtime, and creating a short sequence that signals the day is ending. If you are lying awake for a long time and becoming more frustrated, a quiet low-stimulation activity may be more useful than fighting with the bed.

Persistent or severe sleep problems can have many causes and are worth discussing with a qualified health professional.

## Movement {#movement}

Movement can change energy, attention, and the sense of being stuck. The effective dose is the amount you can realistically do.

Examples:

- walk for five or ten minutes,
- stretch while waiting for a kettle,
- stand up and change rooms,
- do a short mobility routine,
- take stairs for one part of a trip.

If you have medical limitations, pain, dizziness, or exercise restrictions, use guidance appropriate to your health situation.

## Environment reset

Reduce one source of unnecessary friction. Put the item you need where you will see it, silence one nonessential notification, clear enough space to begin a task, or prepare tomorrow's first step before stopping for the night.

::: {.tsk-note}
Wellness is not a moral scorecard. Use these checks to make the system easier to operate, not to create another standard to fail.
:::
